evidence: Checked the entire GRAPH_STATE.md and source at HEAD 1603214845745174f5036ea79375198c7a44a1dd. The alleged omitted mechanisms are real: src/cli/session.rs:61-78 spools caller/session arguments after a failed daemon call; src/transcripts/capture.rs:28-62 writes them under .graph-local/session-spool, syncing file contents before rename. Its registered consumer (src/transcripts/mod.rs:507-509) reads the files before writer admission (capture.rs:254-280), retains them on transient errors (:302-308), and quarantines rejected inputs (:455-462). Separately, the post-commit writer calls worktree::fast_forward (src/writer/mod.rs:409-418), which renames residual dirty/untracked user files from vanished directories into .graph-local/orphans (src/writer/worktree.rs:138-169). Thus neither mechanism can be dismissed as nonexistent or wholly journal-backed. However, this does not contradict the artifact's final stated claims. GRAPH_STATE.md:5 explicitly calls the layout rough, :47 says local operational state 'includes' the listed items, and :47 explicitly establishes that Git-ignored local data can be durable recovery state. It never claims the journal is the only durable local state, that .graph-local contains only metadata, or that this directory can safely be deleted or omitted from backups. The spool fits queued operational ingress and orphans accompany checkout reconciliation; listing either would be a useful optional expansion, but requiring an exhaustive inventory of persistence/ownership categories imports a backup/manual requirement outside this descriptive summary's stated scope. No concrete destructive instruction or materially false statement follows from these omissions. Reject the proposed document-to-code mismatch; no Should-fix/Blocking promotion is supported.
